messages:
Alex (writer): Hey folks, my tiny docs PR updating an example snippet is blocked by the required check `ci/docs-preview/linkcheck`. The action timed out on an external site. Do we have a standard workaround for docs-only flaky linkcheck failures? :grimacing:
Mei L. (docs lead): We try to avoid bypassing checks. Historically we've used either: 1) label-based exemptions for docs-only PRs, or 2) a short-lived manual merge by a maintainer if it's low-risk. Which repo/files did your PR touch?
Alex (writer): Just `/docs/guides/using-sdk.md` and a code sample change, plus one README in `/examples/python/README.md`. No code.
Rohan (platform): If paths are only under `/docs/` and `/examples/` we can treat it as docs-only. We have a GitHub action that can auto-add `docs-auto` label when the diff matches shallow globs, but it was disabled after a mislabeling incident.
merge-bot: ci/docs-preview failed 
  linkcheck: external timeout contacting https://example-external-assets.com (retryable)
  Details: https://github.com/redwood-inference/actions/runs/8912
Alex (writer): Ok — what's the process to get this merged quickly? I don't want to wait for infra changes if it's a one-line copy fix.
Ava (infra): Short-term: I can manually add `docs-auto` label and then a CODEOWNER from `@redwood/docs` needs to approve. Our auto-merge workflow currently refuses to ignore any required status checks; it enforces them all. We can change the workflow to treat `ci/docs-preview/linkcheck` as advisory for PRs with `docs-auto` label, but that needs a small GH Actions change and review.
Mei L. (docs lead): I prefer that change over blanket removal of linkcheck from required checks. Linkcheck catches real regressions. Proposal: re-enable label automation (with stricter path matching), keep linkcheck required, but auto-merge action will allow 'advisory' linkcheck if label present AND at least one human CODEOWNER approved. No single-author bypass.
Rohan (platform): Implementation caveats: branch protection can't be bypassed, so the bot must call the GraphQL merge endpoint with the right checks. Also, label automation must verify the PR isn't from an external contributor and that base branch is `main`. We'll add those guards.
Alex (writer): Who updates CODEOWNERS? I saw we get pinged sometimes from `@redwood/platform` for docs that live near SDK examples. Those extra reviewer requests slow things down.
Ava (infra): Good catch. Current CODEOWNERS snippet is broad. We should narrow it in a follow-up to something like:
/docs/**  @redwood/docs
/examples/sdk/** @redwood/sdk
/ops/** @redwood/platform
That should reduce noisy reviewers for docs-only changes. I'll open a PR to change CODEOWNERS and add `# docs: reduce noisy owners` in the title.
Mei L. (docs lead): Sounds good. For your immediate PR Alex, I'll approve as CODEOWNER once you push a tiny fix I suggested for the snippet. Then @Ava please add `docs-auto` label and Rohan can trigger the merge if other checks are green.
Alex (writer): Pushed the fix. Thanks Mei.
merge-bot: ci/docs-preview 3:45: new run queued. Passing: build, lint. Failing: linkcheck (external timeout)
Ava (infra): I added `docs-auto` label. 
Rohan (platform): @Mei L. thanks for the approve. All required approvals present. Check statuses: build ✅, lint ✅, linkcheck ✖️ (advisory due to docs-auto). I'm invoking the merge queue now.
merge-bot: merge queued by Rohan. Waiting for final merge window.
Alex (writer): Appreciate the fast follow-up. Will file a quick issue to track re-enabling the label automation and the CODEOWNERS cleanup.
Ava (infra): Filing infra/ops PRs now: 1) auto-merge action change behind FF, 2) CODEOWNERS update, 3) re-enable docs-only labelger with stricter globs. I'll tag docs and security for review.
merge-bot: merged commit abc123 into main. CI: all required checks green (linkcheck treated as advisory).
Alex (writer): Merged. Thanks y'all :tada:
